testable_competencies.anatomy: Foundational ear/nose/throat/neck anatomy that frames the rest of the chapter but is not independently tested.

entries.title: Approach to Dizziness and Vertigo (DDx, Peripheral vs. Central Features, Evaluation)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: distinguishing true vertigo from other causes of dizziness and localizing peripheral vs. central vertigo (nystagmus pattern, compensation, associated neurologic signs) is the paradigm case of objective 24's discriminate-the-cause scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Distinguish peripheral from central vertigo (acute continuous onset, abnormal head impulse test, multidirectional nystagmus, skew deviation, or the '5 Ds' of vertebrobasilar insufficiency all suggest a central/dangerous cause requiring urgent neuroimaging) and differentiate true vertigo from cardiac, psychogenic, and other non-vestibular dizziness.

entries.title: Approach to Otalgia (Primary vs. Referred Ear Pain)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 28 explicitly requires a complete head and neck exam 'especially with a normal-appearing ear canal, tympanic membrane, and middle ear' -- i.e. recognizing referred otalgia -- which is exactly this unit's content.

testable_competencies.approach: Distinguish primary otologic causes of ear pain (infection, trauma, cerumen, neoplasm) from referred pain via the sensory innervation of the ear (CN V, VII, IX, X), and recognize that a normal-appearing ear with persistent otalgia warrants a search for a referred source (dental, TMJ, pharyngeal/laryngeal malignancy, temporal arteritis).

entries.title: Approach to Hearing Loss (Physiology, DDx, Bedside Tuning Fork Tests)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 40 explicitly calls out 'differentiating between conductive hearing loss and sensorineural hearing loss', which is exactly the Rinne/Weber bedside-test content here.

testable_competencies.bedside_tests: Perform and interpret the Rinne test (AC vs. BC on the affected ear) and Weber test (lateralization) to distinguish conductive from sensorineural hearing loss at the bedside, and generate an age-appropriate differential for hearing loss (congenital/genetic, infectious, ototoxic, traumatic, neoplastic) before ordering audiometry.

entries.title: Audiometric Testing and Aural Rehabilitation (Pure Tone, Speech, Impedance, ABR, OAE, Hearing Aids)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Interpreting audiometric test results is part of objective 40's diagnostic scope in principle, but the specific test-technology detail here (tympanogram curve typing, ABR wave latencies, OAE mechanism, hearing-aid/cochlear-implant device classification) is specialist audiology/otolaryngology detail beyond graduating-medical-student depth.

testable_competencies.overview: Recognize the existence and general purpose of pure tone, speech, and impedance audiometry, ABR, and OAE testing, and know that hearing-aid/cochlear-implant candidacy decisions are made by audiology/otolaryngology; detailed test interpretation is specialist-level.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK/indirect MCC evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because objective 40's diagnostic scope genuinely touches audiometric testing in principle, even though the test-technology detail itself is not independently sufficient for DIRECT/COMPONENT classification at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 108 explicitly requires diagnosing cause/severity/complications of tinnitus and understanding the distress it causes, matching this unit's full scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize unilateral, pulsatile, or objective tinnitus (audible to the examiner) as requiring further workup (vascular imaging or MRI for acoustic neuroma) rather than routine reassurance, and distinguish subjective (patient-only) tinnitus associated with SNHL from vascular/mechanical causes of objective tinnitus.

entries.title: Approach to Nasal Obstruction (DDx: Acquired vs. Congenital)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is dedicated to nasal obstruction specifically (targeted registry search for 'nasal obstruction' and 'nose' returned zero matches); objective 100's rhinorrhea/upper-airway scope is the closest available anchor for this nasal-symptom differential.

testable_competencies.differential: Generate an age-appropriate differential for nasal obstruction (rhinitis, rhinosinusitis, septal deviation, foreign body, adenoid hypertrophy, and red-flag unilateral obstruction suggesting neoplasm or juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma).

entries.title: Approach to a Neck Mass (DDx by Age, Evaluation)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 63 requires diagnosing the cause of a neck mass with particular attention to excluding malignancy, matching this unit's age-based DDx and evaluation approach.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Reactive lymphadenopathy is the most common inflammatory cause of a neck mass and the DDx explicitly overlaps objective 54's biopsy-decision scope.

testable_competencies.approach: Apply the age-based rule of thumb (congenital <20, inflammatory 20-40, neoplastic >40) and lateral-vs-midline location to generate a differential for a neck mass, and recognize features (hard, fixed, >3 wk duration, associated B symptoms or mucosal lesion) that mandate urgent malignancy workup (FNA, panendoscopy) rather than a trial of antibiotics.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: BPPV is the most common cause of peripheral vertigo and a paradigm case of objective 24's scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_management: Recognize brief, positionally-triggered vertigo as BPPV, confirm with the Dix-Hallpike maneuver, and know first-line treatment is a canalith repositioning maneuver (e.g. Epley) rather than pharmacotherapy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Episodic vertigo attacks are within objective 24's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Progressive fluctuating low-frequency SNHL is a core diagnostic feature within objective 40's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Tinnitus is part of the classic Meniere's tetrad but is not the primary presenting/testable feature here.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize the classic tetrad (episodic vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency SNHL, tinnitus, aural fullness) and know first-line management is a low-salt diet and diuretics before escalation to intratympanic or surgical therapy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute prolonged vertigo without hearing loss (vestibular neuronitis) vs. with hearing loss (labyrinthitis) is a classic vignette within objective 24's discriminate-the-cause scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish vestibular neuronitis (no hearing loss) from labyrinthitis (tinnitus and hearing loss present) after a viral prodrome, and know management is supportive (vestibular suppressants short-term, then vestibular rehabilitation exercises).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Unilateral progressive SNHL is the classic presenting feature and the explicit teaching point 'unilateral tinnitus or SNHL is acoustic neuroma until proven otherwise' is a paradigm case of objective 40's diagnose-the-cause scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Unilateral tinnitus is an alternative presenting symptom within objective 108's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: True vertigo is rare (slow tumour growth allows vestibular compensation); disequilibrium rather than vertigo is more typical, so this is a weaker link than the hearing-loss/tinnitus presentation.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize unilateral progressive SNHL and/or unilateral tinnitus in an adult as acoustic neuroma until proven otherwise, and order gadolinium-enhanced MRI of the internal auditory canal rather than reassurance or routine audiogram alone.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are common non-infectious causes of conductive hearing loss/ear fullness/otalgia within objective 28's differential, and cerumen impaction is a testable indication/contraindication set for ear syringing.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize cerumen impaction as the most common cause of conductive hearing loss in patients 15-50 yr and know indications/contraindications for irrigation (contraindicated with suspected TM perforation or active infection); recognize exostoses as usually incidental findings associated with cold-water swimming.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Otitis externa is one of the most common causes of ear pain seen in primary care and a paradigm case of objective 28's scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_management: Recognize otitis externa by pain on tragal traction/pinna manipulation with EAC edema and erythema, initiate topical antimicrobial therapy (avoiding ototoxic agents such as gentamicin or neomycin if the TM is perforated or status is unknown), and recognize risk factors (water exposure, instrumentation, diabetes).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A limb/life-threatening complication of otitis externa in a specific at-risk population (elderly, diabetic, immunocompromised) that objective 28's 'severity and complications' scope explicitly requires recognizing.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize otalgia and purulent otorrhea refractory to standard otitis externa therapy in an elderly diabetic or immunocompromised patient as malignant otitis externa, a medical emergency requiring temporal bone imaging, hospitalization, and IV antibiotics.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Chronic serous/suppurative otitis media (persistent effusion or perforated-TM drainage) is within objective 28's severity/complications scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish chronic serous otitis media (persistent straw-coloured effusion) from chronic suppurative otitis media (>6 wk purulent drainage through a perforated TM or ventilation tube) and know both warrant ENT referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cholesteatoma is a locally destructive middle-ear mass causing conductive hearing loss and complications (ossicular erosion, labyrinthine fistula, intracranial spread) squarely within objective 28's severity/complications scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a 'small white pearl' behind an intact TM (congenital) or foul-smelling chronic otorrhea with a retraction pocket/perforation (acquired) as cholesteatoma requiring otolaryngology referral for surgical excision given its erosive, complication-prone course.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Mastoiditis is the classic suppurative complication of acute otitis media (postauricular erythema/tenderness with a protruding auricle) within objective 28's complications scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Presents with fever and requires ruling out life-threatening intracranial extension, overlapping objective 107-1's rule-out-serious-cause scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize postauricular erythema, tenderness, and a protruding/displaced auricle following acute otitis media as mastoiditis, requiring urgent imaging (CT) and IV antibiotics +/- mastoidectomy given the risk of intracranial extension.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Otosclerosis is a classic cause of progressive conductive (and later mixed) hearing loss in young adults, within objective 40's differentiate-CHL-from-SNHL scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize progressive conductive hearing loss in a young adult (often with a family history or during pregnancy) with a normal TM as otosclerosis, and know management options range from hearing aids to stapedectomy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 40 explicitly states 'hearing loss in infants must be identified' -- a direct match to congenital SNHL and the importance of universal newborn hearing screening.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Universal newborn hearing screening (otoacoustic emissions/ABR) is part of the standard newborn assessment within objective 74-1's scope.

testable_competencies.screening: Know that universal newborn hearing screening (OAE/ABR) is standard of care because early identification of congenital SNHL (genetic non-syndromic/syndromic, congenital infection, perinatal hypoxia/prematurity) is critical for language development, and that prelingually deaf infants benefit most from early aural rehabilitation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Presbycusis is the most common cause of SNHL in the elderly and a paradigm case of objective 40's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize bilateral, symmetric, high-frequency-predominant SNHL developing with age as presbycusis and know management is hearing amplification rather than a search for a reversible cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Sudden SNHL is a true otologic emergency (idiopathic or otherwise) where delayed treatment worsens prognosis, a paradigm case of objective 40's severity/urgency scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize sudden (typically unilateral) hearing loss as an otologic emergency requiring urgent audiogram and ENT referral for empiric oral or intratympanic corticosteroids within 72 h, rather than watchful waiting.

entries.title: Autoimmune Inner Ear Disease

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A rare cause of rapidly progressive, often bilateral SNHL within objective 40's differential, but individually low-yield/low-prevalence for a generalist exam relative to other SNHL etiologies.

testable_competencies.recognition: Consider autoimmune inner ear disease in rapidly progressive bilateral SNHL, particularly with a background systemic autoimmune condition, and know it may respond to immunosuppression.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Ototoxic medication exposure (aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, platinum chemotherapy, high-dose ASA) is an important, preventable cause of SNHL within objective 40's scope.

testable_competencies.prevention: Recognize aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, platinum-based chemotherapy, and high-dose salicylates as ototoxic and monitor hearing/dose in at-risk patients (e.g. renal impairment, prolonged courses).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A common, preventable cause of SNHL that objective 40 explicitly requires counselling patients about ('educated and counselled on preventing further hearing loss').

testable_competencies.prevention: Recognize occupational/recreational high-volume noise exposure as a cause of bilateral high-frequency (classically 4000 Hz notch) SNHL and counsel on hearing protection as primary prevention.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Temporal bone fracture from head trauma with signs of basilar skull fracture (Battle's sign, raccoon eyes, hemotympanum, CSF otorrhea) is a direct match to objective 109-8's facial/head-trauma scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Immediate complete CN VII palsy after temporal bone trauma is a surgical indication within objective 109-11's nerve-injury scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize signs of basilar skull fracture (Battle's sign, raccoon eyes, CSF oto/rhinorrhea, hemotympanum) after head trauma, avoid instrumenting/syringing the ear canal, and know immediate complete facial nerve palsy after trauma is a surgical indication.

entries.title: Facial Nerve (CN VII) Paralysis (Bell's Palsy vs. Ramsay Hunt Syndrome)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is dedicated to non-traumatic cranial nerve palsy (targeted registry search for 'facial paralysis'/'facial nerve palsy' returned only trauma-oriented objectives); objective 109-11's nerve-injury scope is the closest available anchor, though most peripheral facial paralysis here (Bell's palsy, Ramsay Hunt) is non-traumatic.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish central facial paralysis (forehead-sparing, cross-refer to Neurology) from peripheral facial paralysis (forehead involved), and distinguish Bell's palsy (idiopathic, acute onset, diagnosis of exclusion, treat with corticosteroids +/- antivirals and corneal protection) from Ramsay Hunt syndrome (herpes zoster oticus: vesicles on the pinna/ear canal, hyperacusis, SNHL, worse prognosis, treat with corticosteroids and acyclovir).

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Neurology's cranial neuropathy/peripheral facial palsy objectives (this chapter explicitly redirects central facial paralysis to 'Neurology, N3'); PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK/DISTINCT_CONTEXT designation deferred to the later global cross-chapter ownership audit per project instruction.

entries.title: Rhinitis: Classification and Nasal Discharge Differential

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Classifying rhinitis subtypes and interpreting nasal discharge character is within objective 100's rhinorrhea-diagnosis scope.

testable_competencies.classification: Classify rhinitis as allergic, infectious, vasomotor, atrophic, hormonal, or medicamentosa based on history, and interpret nasal discharge character (watery/mucoid vs. mucopurulent vs. bloody) to guide the differential.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Allergic rhinitis (rhinorrhea, congestion, sneezing) is a paradigm case within objective 100's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: An IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction, directly within objective 4's scope, and commonly co-occurs with other atopic disease.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize allergic rhinitis (nasal itch, watery rhinorrhea, sneezing, congested boggy turbinates, allergic conjunctivitis) and know intranasal corticosteroid is first-line treatment, with allergen avoidance and oral second-generation antihistamines as adjuncts.

entries.title: Vasomotor Rhinitis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A non-allergic rhinitis subtype within objective 100's broad rhinorrhea scope, but individually lower-yield than allergic rhinitis for a generalist exam.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish vasomotor rhinitis (non-allergic triggers: temperature change, alcohol, stress; negative allergy workup) from allergic rhinitis, with management directed at congestion-predominant vs. rhinorrhea-predominant symptoms.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Purulent nasal discharge/congestion with facial pain is within objective 100's rhinorrhea-diagnosis scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recognizing orbital cellulitis/abscess or cavernous sinus thrombosis as a feared complication overlaps objective 107-1's rule-out-serious-cause scope for a febrile patient.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Use symptom-duration criteria (persistent >10 d, worsening after 5 d, or severe symptoms with high fever/purulence for 3-4 d) to distinguish acute bacterial from viral rhinosinusitis, and recognize periorbital swelling, proptosis, or ophthalmoplegia as orbital extension requiring urgent imaging and IV antibiotics.

entries.title: Chronic Rhinosinusitis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Chronic (>12 wk) sinonasal inflammation is within objective 100's broad scope, but detailed endoscopic sinus surgery decision-making is specialist-level.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize chronic rhinosinusitis (>12 wk of symptoms) and its predisposing factors (anatomic obstruction, immune/systemic disease, cystic fibrosis, immotile cilia syndromes) and know refractory cases are referred for endoscopic sinus surgery.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is dedicated to epistaxis specifically (targeted registry search for 'epistaxis' and 'nosebleed' returned zero matches); objective 15-1's bleeding-diagnosis scope is the closest available anchor for this very high-prevalence ENT presentation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Traumatic epistaxis (nasal fracture, septal injury) overlaps objective 109-8's facial-trauma scope.

testable_competencies.management: Manage anterior epistaxis (most common, Kiesselbach's plexus) with direct pressure and topical vasoconstrictor/cautery, and recognize posterior epistaxis (more common in elderly/hypertensive patients, higher-volume bleeding) as requiring posterior packing, admission, and ENT involvement; know recurrent unilateral epistaxis in an adolescent male raises concern for juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma.

entries.title: Approach to Hoarseness (DDx, Red Flags for Laryngoscopy)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is dedicated to hoarseness/voice change (targeted registry search for 'hoarseness' and 'voice' returned zero matches); objective 100's upper-airway-symptom scope is the closest available anchor.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Generate a differential for hoarseness by category (infectious, traumatic/iatrogenic, neoplastic, neurologic vocal cord paralysis) and recognize that hoarseness persisting >2-3 wk, especially with smoking/alcohol history, warrants laryngoscopy to exclude malignancy.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Laryngitis (usually viral, self-limited hoarseness) falls within the broad upper-respiratory-symptom family anchored by objective 100, though no dedicated objective exists.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize acute laryngitis as usually viral and self-limited (voice rest, hydration) and chronic laryngitis (lifestyle: smoking, reflux) as warranting risk-factor modification and laryngoscopy if persistent.

entries.title: Vocal Cord Polyps and Nodules

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Benign vocal-fold lesions causing hoarseness fall within the broad upper-airway-symptom family anchored by objective 100, though no dedicated objective exists.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish vocal cord nodules (bilateral, chronic voice abuse, e.g. teachers/singers) from polyps (usually unilateral, single episode of vocal strain or smoking) and know first-line management is voice therapy.

entries.title: Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize HPV-related recurrent respiratory papillomatosis as a rare cause of progressive hoarseness/airway obstruction in a child, managed by serial specialist debulking.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is dedicated to laryngeal/head-and-neck cancer specifically beyond the neck-mass/thyroid objective; objective 100's upper-airway scope is the closest anchor for the presenting hoarseness symptom, but the project's explicit inclusion of 'recognition of malignancy warning features' supports retaining this as a DIRECT recognition unit despite weak direct MCC evidence.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize persistent hoarseness (>2-3 wk) in a patient with smoking/alcohol use as a red flag for laryngeal carcinoma requiring laryngoscopy and biopsy, rather than symptomatic treatment.

entries.title: Sialadenitis and Sialolithiasis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Salivary gland swelling/infection is anatomically adjacent to objective 63's neck-mass scope but not a direct match; no dedicated salivary-gland objective exists (targeted registry search for 'salivary gland' returned zero matches).

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize acute sialadenitis (painful, tender, warm gland swelling, often bacterial or viral) and sialolithiasis (postprandial pain and swelling from a duct stone) and know first-line management is conservative (hydration, sialagogues, massage) with surgery reserved for recurrent/refractory cases.

entries.title: Salivary Gland Neoplasms (incl. Parotid Gland Neoplasms)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A salivary gland mass is a form of neck/facial mass within objective 63's exclude-malignancy scope, particularly given the teaching point that facial nerve (CN VII) palsy with a parotid mass strongly suggests malignancy.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize that the smaller the salivary gland, the higher the likelihood a mass within it is malignant (parotid masses are usually benign; minor salivary gland masses are usually malignant), and that facial nerve (CN VII) palsy with a parotid mass is a red flag for malignant invasion requiring urgent workup (FNA, imaging).

entries.title: Branchial Cleft Cysts, Sinuses, and Fistulae

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A classic lateral congenital neck mass within objective 63's diagnose-the-cause-of-a-neck-mass scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A congenital anomaly of branchial arch/pouch development within objective 36-2's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a lateral neck cyst/sinus/fistula (classically anterior to the sternocleidomastoid) as a branchial cleft anomaly and know it should be surgically excised rather than incised and drained if infected.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The classic midline congenital neck mass and a paradigm case of objective 63's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a midline neck mass that elevates with tongue protrusion/swallowing as a thyroglossal duct cyst, and know pre-operative thyroid ultrasound is required to confirm the presence of a normally located thyroid gland before surgical excision (Sistrunk procedure).

entries.title: Lymphatic, Venous, or Mixed Venolymphatic Malformations

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A congenital vascular/lymphatic neck mass within objective 63's broad scope, but individually low-yield relative to more common congenital neck masses.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A vestigial lymphatic-channel malformation within objective 36-2's congenital-anomaly scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a soft, compressible neck mass present since infancy (macrocystic) or with mucosal/skin vesicles (microcystic) as a lymphatic/venolymphatic malformation, and know acute infection-related enlargement should not prompt immediate surgery.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Head and Neck Malignancy: Pre-Malignant Lesions, Risk Factors, and General Approach

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: General H&N cancer risk-factor/screening content overlaps objective 63's exclude-malignancy scope for a neck mass but is broader than that single objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cervical lymphadenopathy is the presenting sign for many H&N malignancies, overlapping objective 54's biopsy-decision scope.

testable_competencies.risk_factors: Recognize leukoplakia, erythroplakia, and oral lichen planus as pre-malignant oral lesions requiring biopsy/follow-up, and know the major modifiable H&N cancer risk factors (smoking, alcohol -- synergistic with smoking -- and oral HPV infection, independent of tobacco/alcohol).

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK/indirect MCC evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because objectives 63 and 54 genuinely touch H&N-malignancy risk-factor recognition even though neither is an exact match for this general-overview unit; the disease-specific evidence lives on SU-OT-45 (Thyroid Carcinoma) and the neck-mass units instead.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A near-exact match: objective 63 is titled 'Neck masses and thyroid disease' and explicitly requires excluding malignancy in a thyroid mass.

testable_competencies.approach: Apply the standard thyroid nodule workup (serum TSH plus thyroid ultrasound, with FNA guided by ultrasound risk features/size), recognize papillary carcinoma as the most common and generally favourable-prognosis subtype, and recognize red flags (rapidly enlarging mass, hoarseness, dysphagia, family history of MEN II) suggesting a more aggressive subtype (medullary, anaplastic).

entries.title: Acute Otitis Media and Otitis Media with Effusion (Pediatric)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute otitis media is the most common cause of ear pain and most frequent reason for pediatric antibiotic prescribing, a paradigm case of objective 28's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: AOM is a very common source of fever in young children within objective 107-1's rule-out-cause scope.

testable_competencies.management: Diagnose AOM (bulging/erythematous TM with acute symptoms) vs. OME (effusion without acute infection), apply watchful-waiting vs. immediate-antibiotic criteria by age and severity, and recognize predisposing anatomic/craniofacial risk factors for recurrent AOM.

entries.title: Adenoid Hypertrophy

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Adenoid hypertrophy is a major contributor to pediatric sleep-disordered breathing within objective 98's scope, though it is more often assessed as one cause within SU-OT-48 than tested independently.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize mouth breathing, hyponasal speech, snoring, and recurrent otitis media/rhinosinusitis as features of adenoid hypertrophy, and know adenoidectomy is considered for refractory cases or associated sleep-disordered breathing.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

entries.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing in Children (incl. Obstructive Sleep Apnea)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pediatric OSA/sleep-disordered breathing (snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime hyperactivity/inattention) is a direct match to objective 98's diagnose-and-manage sleep disorder scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize snoring, witnessed apneic pauses, restless sleep, and daytime behavioural/learning problems as pediatric sleep-disordered breathing, most commonly due to adenotonsillar hypertrophy, and know adenotonsillectomy is first-line treatment when hypertrophy is the cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A severe complication of pharyngitis/tonsillitis and a classic 'severity and complications' teaching case within objective 100's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Presents with fever as part of the systemic infectious picture, overlapping objective 107-1's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize trismus, muffled ('hot potato') voice, uvular deviation, and drooling on a background of severe unilateral sore throat as peritonsillar abscess, requiring urgent needle aspiration/incision and drainage plus antibiotics rather than outpatient management as simple pharyngitis.

entries.title: Tonsillectomy (Indications)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recurrent severe pharyngitis/tonsillitis frequency criteria for tonsillectomy overlap objective 100's scope, but the surgical-indication threshold itself is a specialist/surgical decision point rather than a generalist diagnostic competency.

testable_competencies.indications: Know the general categories of tonsillectomy indication (recurrent/severe pharyngotonsillitis meeting frequency criteria, obstructive sleep-disordered breathing, suspected malignancy) without needing to apply exact frequency thresholds.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.
entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK/indirect MCC evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because objective 100's scope genuinely touches recurrent pharyngitis, which is the main driver for this surgical indication, even though the indication threshold itself is specialist-level.

entries.title: Airway Problems in Children and Signs of Airway Obstruction

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recognizing signs of upper airway obstruction (stridor, retractions, tripod positioning) in a child and correctly triaging severity by respiratory rate for age is a direct match to objective 27-3's scope.

testable_competencies.triage: Recognize signs of impending airway obstruction in a child (stridor, drooling, tripod positioning, retractions, cyanosis) and apply the general principle of minimizing agitation/avoiding unnecessary exam maneuvers (e.g. tongue depressor) that could precipitate complete obstruction in a child with a tenuous airway.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Croup (barky cough, inspiratory stridor, viral, typically parainfluenza) is a paradigm case of pediatric upper-airway respiratory distress within objective 27-3's scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize the barky cough, hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor of croup, grade severity by the Westley score/clinical impression, and initiate dexamethasone +/- nebulized epinephrine for moderate-severe cases while reserving hospitalization for refractory or severe presentations.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Epiglottitis is a true pediatric airway emergency (rapid-onset stridor, drooling, tripod/sniffing position, toxic appearance) within objective 27-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: High fever with toxic appearance is part of the classic presentation, within objective 107-1's rule-out-life-threatening-cause scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize rapid-onset high fever, drooling, muffled voice, and tripod/sniffing positioning as epiglottitis, avoid agitating the child or examining the oropharynx/using a tongue depressor (risk of precipitating complete obstruction), and secure the airway in a controlled setting (OR) before further workup.

entries.title: Subglottic Stenosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A less common structural cause of pediatric stridor/respiratory distress within objective 27-3's broad scope, individually lower-yield than croup/epiglottitis/laryngomalacia.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize recurrent/persistent stridor in a child with a history of prolonged intubation as acquired subglottic stenosis, or as congenital in an infant with no such history.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, foundational-background, or low-yield/no-dedicated-MCC-objective content; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Laryngomalacia is the most common cause of stridor in infancy, within objective 27-3's differential-diagnosis scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize inspiratory stridor worsening with feeding/supine positioning and improving prone in an otherwise well infant as laryngomalacia, and know most cases resolve spontaneously by 12-18 mo with surgery (supraglottoplasty) reserved for severe cases (failure to thrive, apnea).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute-onset choking/stridor/respiratory distress from an inhaled foreign body is within objective 27-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: An aspirated/ingested foreign body is a mechanical airway emergency loosely within objective 109's broad trauma-management scope, though not classic trauma.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize sudden-onset choking, unilateral wheeze, or asymmetric breath sounds in a toddler as suspicious for an inhaled foreign body, and know rigid bronchoscopy (not blind finger sweeps) is the definitive management for a witnessed or strongly suspected airway foreign body.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A serious, potentially airway- and mediastinum-threatening infection presenting with fever, within objective 107-1's rule-out-life-threatening-cause scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Presents as a tender, often fluctuant neck swelling, overlapping objective 63's neck-mass scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize fever, neck swelling/torticollis, trismus, and odynophagia as concerning for deep neck space infection (retropharyngeal, parapharyngeal, or submandibular/Ludwig's angina), requiring urgent contrast CT imaging and airway assessment given the risk of airway compromise and descending mediastinitis.
